## Description
Since the move to the unified Google GenAI SDK in 4.0.0, model
generation parameters like `max_output_tokens`, `temperature`, `top_k`,
... were not passed through to the actual request. They were created as
part of the `params` object, but only select params were actually passed
through.
This is an important fix, because currently the only way to pass these
generation parameters is by adding them when calling the `invoke`
method. However, this happens silently, and someone setting for example
`temperature` at the model level, would not detect this immediately and
hence would not be aware of the problem. Only `max_output_tokens` is
relatively easy to detect when there are too many tokens in the output.
This PR fixes the issue, and makes the code easier to maintain, by
making sure all `params` are passed through without having to enumerate
them manually. This required moving some of the manipulation steps into
the `_build_base_generation_config` method where they sit more
naturally.
## Relevant issues
Fixes #1454
## Type
🐛 Bug Fix
## Changes
Pass through all `params` to `_build_request_config`.
To avoid having to enumerate all params in multiple places, leverage the
model's Pydantic model dumping capabilities.
This required a couple of adjustments:
- When creating the `GenerateContentConfig` in `_build_request_config`,
remove all parameters that are included in `params`. This allows us to
consume the whole `params` object without duplicating parameters.
- This required moving some preparation steps for these parameters from
this method to `_build_base_generation_config`, where they sit more
naturally:
- Convert `response_modalities` to their values.
- Auto-set audio output for TTS models if not explicitly configured.
- Create the `ThinkingConfig` object if needed.
- Change `_build_thinking_config` to return a `ThinkingConfig`` object
instead of a dict, reducing the need to do the conversion later.
## Testing(optional)
- Changed the model initialization test to capture the failure, checking
the config coming out of `_prepare_request` in line with other tests.
- Adapted the tests that check that model parameters can be overridden
to also check `_prepare_request` rather than the earlier
`_prepare_params` step. This to capture any regressions that might be
introduced by changing the flow as described in the changes.

feat(genai): support optional `seed` parameter (#1437)
Credit to @Odessit007 for the original implementation.
Adds support for an optional `seed` parameter to
`ChatGoogleGenerativeAI` and `GoogleGenerativeAI`, enabling more
reproducible generations when desired.
The Google GenAI SDK exposes a `seed` parameter for reproducible
generations, but `langchain-google-genai` previously lacked this
functionality. This feature allows users to get more deterministic
outputs when needed for testing, debugging, or reproducibility
requirements.
## Usage
```python
from langchain_google_genai import ChatGoogleGenerativeAI
# With seed for reproducible outputs
llm = ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(
model="gemini-2.5-flash",
seed=42,
)
# Without seed (default behavior - random seed each time)
llm = ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(
model="gemini-2.5-flash",
)
```
> [!NOTE]
> Using the same seed does not guarantee identical outputs, but makes
them more deterministic.
>
> Reproducibility is "best effort" based on the model and
infrastructure.
- This revives the changes from PR #1356 which was accidentally closed

Thinking parameters were only sent to the API if the model's profile
indicated reasoning_output: True. For models without a profile entry,
this caused `include_thoughts`, `thinking_budget`, and `thinking_level`
to be silently ignored—even when the model actually supported thinking.
This change removes the profile check, ensuring user-provided thinking
config is always forwarded to the API. Unsupported models will now
receive proper API errors instead of silent failures.

message:
fix(vertexai): fix "Object of type 'FieldInfo' is not JSON serializable" across all schema generation (#1317)
## Description
Fixes "TypeError: Object of type 'FieldInfo' is not JSON serializable"
that occurred when using with_structured_output(..., method="json_mode")
with Pydantic v2 models containing Field metadata.
The issue occurred because model_json_schema() was called without the
mode parameter, causing Pydantic v2 to use validation mode which can
include non-serializable FieldInfo objects in certain contexts. Adding
mode='serialization' tells Pydantic to use its serialization schema
generation mode, which properly handles FieldInfo objects.
Using mode='serialization' is also semantically correct since the schema
describes the model's output format (what Gemini should generate), not
input validation rules.
Changes:
- Add mode='serialization' to model_json_schema() in chat_models.py:2562
- Add unit test for Pydantic v2 FieldInfo serialization
- Add unit test for Pydantic v1 backward compatibility
- Verify both Pydantic v1 (schema() method) and v2 paths work correctly
Backward compatibility:
- Pydantic v1 models: Continue using schema() method (line 2560)
- Pydantic v2 models: Now use model_json_schema(mode='serialization')
- No public API changes, fully backward compatible

feat(vertexai): add default dimensions parameter to VertexAIEmbeddings (#1242)
## Summary
Add optional `dimensions` constructor argument to `VertexAIEmbeddings`
class. This allows users to set a default output dimensionality that
will be used for all embedding requests unless explicitly overridden.
## Changes
- Add `dimensions` field to `VertexAIEmbeddings` with default value
`None`
- Update `embed()` method to use constructor default when dimensions not
specified in method call
- Explicit dimensions in method calls override the constructor default
- Full backward compatibility maintained - existing code continues to
work unchanged
## Usage Example
```python
# Set default dimensions in constructor
embeddings = VertexAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-004", dimensions=128)
# Uses 128 dimensions (from constructor)
embeddings.embed(["hello", "world"])
# Overrides with 256 dimensions
embeddings.embed(["hello", "world"], dimensions=256)
# Backward compatible - no dimensions specified
embeddings = VertexAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-004")
embeddings.embed(["hello", "world"])  # Uses model's default
```
## Test Plan
- [x] Added 5 new unit tests covering all scenarios
- [x] Test that constructor dimensions are used when not specified in
embed()
- [x] Test that explicit dimensions override constructor default
- [x] Test backward compatibility when no default dimensions specified

embed_query()

author: Yashwant Bezawada
message:
fix(genai): Add validation for empty contents in Gemini API requests (#1298)
## Summary
Fixes issue where invoking `ChatGoogleGenerativeAI` with only a
`SystemMessage` causes a cryptic 400 error from the Gemini API.
**Related Issue:** langchain-ai/langgraph#6413
## Problem
The Gemini API requires at least one non-system message (content) in the
request. When only a `SystemMessage` is provided:
1. The message gets extracted as `system_instruction` in
`_parse_chat_history()`
2. The `contents` array becomes empty
3. The Gemini API rejects the request with: `"Invalid argument provided
to Gemini: 400 * GenerateContentRequest.contents: contents is not
specified"`
## Solution
This PR adds validation after message parsing to check if the `history`
(contents) array is empty and raises a clear `ValueError` with
actionable guidance:
```python
# Validate that we have at least one content message for the API
if not history:
msg = (
"No content messages found. The Gemini API requires at least one "
"non-system message (HumanMessage, AIMessage, etc.). "
"If you only have a SystemMessage, please set "
"convert_system_message_to_human=True when initializing the model, "
"or include additional messages in your input."
)
raise ValueError(msg)
```
## Changes
- Added validation in `_prepare_request()` method (lines 2353-2362)
- Added two unit tests:
- `test_system_message_only_raises_error()` - Verifies the error is
raised
- `test_system_message_with_convert_flag_works()` - Verifies the
workaround works
## Testing
The fix includes comprehensive unit tests that verify:
1. A `ValueError` is raised when only a `SystemMessage` is provided
2. The error message guides users to the correct solution
3. The workaround (`convert_system_message_to_human=True`) works
correctly
## Backward Compatibility
This change is backward compatible:
- No changes to existing successful use cases
- Only affects the edge case of passing only a `SystemMessage`, which
previously failed with a cryptic error
- Now fails fast with a helpful error message

author: Yashwant Bezawada
message:
fix(genai): use `task_type_to_use` variable in `embed_query` methods (#1302)
Fixes #1299
## Summary
The `embed_query` and `aembed_query` methods in
`GoogleGenerativeAIEmbeddings` were calculating `task_type_to_use` with
a default value of `"RETRIEVAL_QUERY"` when `task_type=None`, but then
passing the original `task_type` parameter (which is `None`) to
`_prepare_request()`, causing the default to be ignored.
## Changes
- **libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/embeddings.py**
- Line 342: Changed `task_type=task_type,` to
`task_type=task_type_to_use,` in `embed_query` method
- Line 435: Changed `task_type=task_type,` to
`task_type=task_type_to_use,` in `aembed_query` method
- **libs/genai/tests/unit_tests/test_embeddings.py**
- Added `test_embed_query_default_task_type()` to verify default
`RETRIEVAL_QUERY` is used when `task_type=None`
## Root Cause
Both methods followed this pattern:
```python
task_type_to_use = task_type if task_type else self.task_type
if task_type_to_use is None:
task_type_to_use = "RETRIEVAL_QUERY"
request = self._prepare_request(
text=text,
task_type=task_type,  # ❌ Bug: passing None instead of "RETRIEVAL_QUERY"
...
)
```
## Impact
When users call `embed_query()` or `aembed_query()` without specifying a
`task_type` parameter (and the instance doesn't have a default
`task_type`), the API receives `task_type=None` instead of the intended
default `"RETRIEVAL_QUERY"`.
## Test Plan
- ✅ Added regression test `test_embed_query_default_task_type()`
- ✅ Verified syntax with `python3 -m py_compile`
- ✅ CI will run full test suite including existing embedding tests
---------
Co-authored-by: Mason Daugherty <github@mdrxy.com>

# Add Google Sheets read-only tools and toolkit
Add Google Sheets read-only integration to the community package,
providing tools for reading spreadsheet data with dual authentication
support and error handling.
## Type
🆕 New Feature
✅ Test
## Changes
Add Google Sheets read-only tools for LangChain integration
- **SheetsBaseTool** — abstract base with dual auth (API key / OAuth2)
- **SheetsReadDataTool** — read a single range with flexible formatting
- **SheetsBatchReadDataTool** — read multiple ranges in one call
- **SheetsFilteredReadDataTool** — filter data with multiple condition
types
- **SheetsGetSpreadsheetInfoTool** — access spreadsheet
metadata/properties
- **SheetsToolkit** — curated tool bundle
Error handling
- Type hints
- Support for both API key and OAuth2 authentication
- Data formatting options
- Error messages and validation
Add supporting infrastructure
- **enums.py** — constants for Sheets API options
- **utils.py** — service builder and auth helpers
- **urls.py** — endpoint definitions
- **base.py** — authentication and service management
Add integration tests
- Unit tests for all tools
- Integration tests with actual API calls
- Error handling scenarios
- Authentication flow tests
## Testing
✅ All checks passed:
Test scenarios covered:
- Single range data reading
- Batch range operations
- Filtered data queries
- Spreadsheet metadata access
- API key authentication
- OAuth2 authentication
- Error handling with invalid inputs
## Note
Requires GOOGLE_SHEETS_API_KEY environment variable for API key
authentication
All tests pass locally
Follows community package standards
Error handling for API responses
Type hints included
Supports both API key and OAuth2 authentication
Compatible with LangChain agents and toolkits
Read-only scope - write operations will come in a follow-up PR

## PR Description
<!-- e.g. "Implement user authentication feature" -->
- When using ChatGoogleGenerativeAI with tools that have parameters
typed as unions with None (e.g., list[str] | None), the field
descriptions and enum values are not being passed to the Gemini model.
This occurs because the schema conversion process loses critical field
properties when handling anyOf JSON schema structures.
## Relevant issues
<!-- e.g. "Fixes #000" -->
Fixes: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-google/issues/1091
## Type
<!-- Select the type of Pull Request -->
<!-- Keep only the necessary ones -->
🐛 Bug Fix
## Changes(optional)
<!-- List of changes -->
- **Preserve field descriptions**: Preserve description before any
schema manipulation. Maintain existing behaviour of preferring the
description from the filtered schema, but fall back to original
description if not present.
- **Preserve enum values**: When handling anyOf schemas for nullable
union types, preserve original enum and items properties that would
otherwise be lost during schema filtering.
- **Enhanced items schema processing**: Added enum preservation in
`_get_items_from_schema` to ensure array item constraints (like Literal
types) are properly passed to Gemini.
- **Extended schema filtering**: Added handling for all anyOf types (not
just arrays/objects) to preserve enums in nullable string literals like
`Optional[Literal["A", "B", "C"]]`.
This fix ensures that field descriptions, enum constraints, and array
item specifications are properly preserved and passed to Google Gemini
models when using Union types with None, enabling proper function
calling with constrained parameters.
## Testing(optional)
<!-- Test procedure -->
- **Unit Tests**: All unit tests pass, including specific
`test_function_utils.py` tests that validate schema preservation
- **Integration Tests**: Previously failing CI tests now pass:
- `test_tool_calling_async` - (was failing in initial commit due to
missing enum constraints)
- `test_structured_output[typeddict]` - (was failing in initial commit
due to lost field descriptions)
- **Schema Validation**: Verified enum preservation for
`Optional[Literal["A", "B", "C"]]` types
- **Backward Compatibility**: Confirmed all existing functionality
remains intact
<!-- Test result -->
- **Before fix**: Descriptions and enum values were lost during anyOf
schema processing, resulting in unconstrained parameters and failed tool
calls
- **After fix**: Descriptions and enum values are properly preserved for
all nullable union types, enabling correct function calling with
constrained parameters
## Note(optional)
<!-- Information about the errors fixed by PR -->
The original issue only affected nullable union types with specific
constraints (enums, literals). Regular non-nullable fields and simple
nullable fields without constraints were unaffected. This fix
specifically targets the anyOf schema processing logic to ensure all
field metadata is preserved during schema transformation.

search tool responses.

message:
Fix Gemini schema validation errors for Union and Optional[Dict] types (#1143)
This PR fixes two critical Gemini API schema validation errors that
occur when using Pydantic models with Union types and Optional[Dict]
fields in `ChatGoogleGenerativeAI.with_structured_output()` and
`bind_tools()`.
## Issues Fixed
### 1. Union Types Getting Invalid `type_` Assignment
**Error:**
`GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[0].parameters.properties[action].type:
must be specified`
```python
class Response(BaseModel):
response: str
class Act(BaseModel):
action: Union[Response, Plan] = Field(description="Action to perform")
# Before: action.type_ = 0 (invalid)
# After: action.type_ = 6 (OBJECT)
```
### 2. Optional[Dict] Types Getting Incorrect STRING Type
**Error:**
`GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[0].parameters.properties[params].properties:
should be non-empty for OBJECT type`
```python
class RequestsGetToolInput(BaseModel):
params: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = Field(default={}, description="Query parameters")
# Before: params.type_ = 1 (STRING)
# After: params.type_ = 6 (OBJECT), nullable=True
```
## Root Cause
The issues were in `_get_properties_from_schema()` function in
`_function_utils.py`:
1. **Union types**: When processing `anyOf` schemas with all non-null
types, the code created an `anyOf` property but never set a `type_`
field, leaving it as 0 (invalid for Gemini)
2. **Optional[Dict] types**: Objects with `additionalProperties` but no
`properties` were incorrectly converted to STRING type instead of
maintaining OBJECT type
3. **Missing descriptions**: Descriptions were extracted after schema
modifications, losing the original description from nullable schemas
## Changes Made
1. **Fix Union type assignment**: Ensure non-nullable `anyOf` schemas
get proper `type_` assignment in addition to `anyOf` property
2. **Fix Optional[Dict] handling**: Only convert objects to STRING type
if they have neither `properties` nor `additionalProperties`
3. **Fix description preservation**: Extract descriptions before any
schema modifications to preserve them
4. **Add regression tests**: Comprehensive test coverage to prevent
these issues from reoccurring
## Testing
The fix has been validated with:
- Direct reproduction of the original error cases
- Integration with `ChatGoogleGenerativeAI.with_structured_output()` and
`bind_tools()`
- Comprehensive regression tests added to the test suite
- All existing function utility tests continue to pass
Fixes #535.

## PR Description
Include the `prompt_feedback` in the `response_metadata` of the
`AIMessageChunk` when content is blocked during streaming.
This fix addresses the inconsistency between streaming and non-streaming
responses when content is blocked by Gemini's safety filters. Without
this fix, applications cannot distinguish between network errors, API
issues, and content policy violations in streaming scenarios.
### Benefits
1. **Consistency**: Streaming responses now provide the same safety
information as non-streaming responses
2. **Programmatic Access**: Applications can detect blocked content via
`chunk.response_metadata.get("prompt_feedback")`
3. **Better UX**: Downstream applications can show users specific error
messages instead of generic "empty response" errors
4. **Minimal Impact**: No breaking changes to existing API behavior
## Relevant issues
Fixes: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-google/issues/1103
## Type
🐛 Bug Fix
## Changes
**File:** `langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py`
**Lines:** 818-822
**Before:**
```python
if stream:
generations = [
ChatGenerationChunk(
message=AIMessageChunk(content=""), generation_info={}
)
]
```
**After:**
```python
if stream:
generations = [
ChatGenerationChunk(
message=AIMessageChunk(
content="",
response_metadata={"prompt_feedback": proto.Message.to_dict(response.prompt_feedback)}
),
generation_info={}
)
]
```
## Testing
In addition to existing tests, the change has been manually smoke tested
with:
- Normal streaming responses (no regression)
- Blocked content scenarios (now includes prompt_feedback)
- Non-streaming responses (unchanged behavior)

author: open-swe[bot]
message:
fix: Add field alias for `default_metadata` in `ChatGoogleGenerativeAI` (#1061)
Fixes #1060
## Issue Description
LangSmith Playground fails to rehydrate traces for
`ChatGoogleGenerativeAI`.
This occurs when users click "Playground" on successful traces in the
LangSmith UI. The issue stems from a serialization/deserialization
mismatch where LangSmith passes `null` values that the original field
definition couldn't accept.
## Root Cause
The issue occurs due to the serialization flow:
1. Normal usage: `default_metadata` is set to `()` (empty tuple)
2. Trace serialization: Gets serialized and potentially converted to
null during LangSmith's storage/transmission pipeline
3. Playground reconstruction: LangSmith attempts
`ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(default_metadata_input=null)`
4. Validation failure: The original field definition
`Sequence[Tuple[str, str]]` rejects `null` values
## Changes Made
- Changed `default_metadata` type from `Sequence[Tuple[str, str]]` to
`Optional[Sequence[Tuple[str, str]]]`
- Added `alias="default_metadata_input"` to maintain compatibility with
LangSmith's serialization
- Preserved behavior: The validator ensures the field always resolves to
a proper tuple value, even when `None` is passed
- Created `test_default_metadata_field_alias()` to verify the fix works
with various input scenarios

message:
vertexai[patch]: support thought signatures in function calls (#1025)
Gemini docs for feature:
https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking#signatures
Here we just support for function calls. Resulting AIMessages keep an
association between tool call IDs and thought signatures, stored as a
base64 string:
```python
AIMessage(
content=[...],
tool_calls=[
{
"type": "tool_call",
"id": "abc_123",
"name": "my_tool",
"args": {"param1": "value1", "param2": "value2"},
}
],
additional_kwargs={
"__gemini_function_call_thought_signatures__": {
"abc_123": _bytes_to_base64(b"thought signature bytes")
}
},
)
```
Thought signatures can also exist on text parts when (1) thinking is
enabled, and (2) tools are bound. These will likely break
interoperability of messages across chat models, so support there is
blocked by an ongoing effort to move to standardized content blocks
(high priority / ongoing now).

message:
Change post-filters to pre-filters in BigQueryVectorStore (#554)
BigQueryVectorStore's _create_filters are post-filters. Now that BigQuery Vector Search supports pre-filtering on stored columns (https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/vector-index#stored-columns), we can change all post-filters to pre-filters.
Note that this requires storing the columns that are referenced by the pre-filter. This cannot be done in Langchain yet. If the required columns are not stored, then the pre-filters will act as post-filters. The results returned by the new post-filters will be a superset of the post-filters done currently, which can return less results.
